title: You Are What You Annotate: Towards Better Models through Annotator Representations

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's Kappa) and analyzing label disagreements between Muslim immigrant annotators and non-Muslim annotators on a Brexit-related hate speech dataset.
Performing K-means clustering on learned annotation embeddings and mapping the resulting clusters to the political identification of the annotators (e.g., very liberal to very conservative).
Clustering annotation embeddings from a sentiment analysis dataset and mapping the clusters to the prevalent age ranges of the annotators to identify age-related labeling tendencies.
Mapping K-means clusters of annotator representations to annotator education levels and annual household income to identify systemic differences in annotation behavior.
Correlating learned annotation embedding clusters with the self-reported gender of annotators to evaluate demographic alignments in subjective NLP tasks.
Analyzing annotation embedding clusters against annotators' geographic backgrounds, specifically comparing rural, suburban, and urban living and upbringing environments.
